candidates.title: SMILES. 2. Algorithm for generation of unique SMILES notation
candidates.basis: Weininger et al. 1989: replaces each atom rank by a prime and takes products over neighbours to refine canonical ranks; prime codes used for canonical naming only, no partitioning property.

candidates.title: Atomic ring invariant and Modified CANON extended connectivity algorithm for symmetry perception in molecular graphs and rigorous canonicalization of SMILES
candidates.basis: Krotko 2020 (abstract read): product of primes for ring sizes as an atom invariant for canonicalisation; no log P / log Kow.

candidates.title: A canonical ordering of polybenzenes and polymantanes using a prime number factorization technique
candidates.basis: Elk 1990: prime-factorisation code used to give canonical names to polybenzenes/polymantanes; nomenclature only.

candidates.title: Expansion of Matula Numbers to Heteroatoms and to Ring Compounds
candidates.basis: Elk 1995: extends prime-factorisation (Matula) codes to heteroatoms and rings; title and citing works place it in nomenclature; abstract not readable (ACS HTTP 403), so heteroatom weighting scheme and any property use unverified.

candidates.title: Further Properties Derivable from the Matula Number of an Alkane
candidates.basis: Elk & Gutman 1994: per citing work (Deutsch 2012), the 'properties' are graph statistics of the alkane tree read from its Matula number, not physicochemical data; abstract not read.

candidates.title: On Matula numbers
candidates.basis: Gutman & Ivić 1996: mathematical properties of the prime-based tree code motivated by alkane coding; no partitioning.

candidates.title: Matula Numbers and their Applications
candidates.basis: Dossou-Olory & Mojeed 2025 review (chapter read): chemistry applications listed are nomenclature and information retrieval only; no log P, boiling point or QSPR.

candidates.title: Matula numbers, Gödel numbering and Fock space
candidates.basis: Neto 2013 (abstract read): Gödel-type relabelling links rooted-tree codes to Fock space; no physicochemical property.

candidates.title: Molecular Connectivity III: Relationship to Partition Coefficients
candidates.basis: Murray, Hall & Kier 1975: degree-based connectivity index correlated with partition coefficients; nearest descriptor-vs-log P work, but not a prime code.

candidates.title: Modeling the Octanol−Water Partition Coefficients by an Optimized Molecular Connectivity Index
candidates.basis: Šoškić & Plavšić 2005: connectivity index with optimised atom weights fitted to log Kow; fitted weights, not fixed prime weights.

candidates.title: Calculation of Molecular Lipophilicity: State-of-the-Art and Comparison of LogP Methods on more than 96,000 Compounds
candidates.basis: Mannhold et al. 2009: log P from carbon and heteroatom counts alone; an element-count size baseline close to what log10(code) measures, no prime code.

candidates.title: Notes on quantitative structure-properties relationships (QSPR) part 2: The role of the number of atoms as a molecular descriptor
candidates.basis: Carbó-Dorca & Saliner 2009 (abstract read): atom count as QSPR descriptor; size-type descriptor, no prime code, log Kow not the stated focus.

candidates.title: DNA coding and Gödel numbering
candidates.basis: Nicolaidis & Psomopoulos 2022: Gödel number of a nucleotide sequence, not an atom-level molecular graph; no partitioning.

candidates.title: Hosoya Polynomials of Power Graphs of Certain Finite Groups
candidates.basis: Primes index group orders of algebraic graphs; no molecules or log P.

candidates.title: A novel descriptor of molecular graphs and its implications in QSPR studies of antiviral drugs
candidates.basis: Malik & Noureen 2026: augmented Sombor (degree-based) index vs drug properties; no prime code, log Kow not reported in the abstract seen.

candidates.title: SMILES. 2. Algorithm for generation of unique SMILES notation (Weininger, Weininger, Weininger 1989)
candidates.basis: CANON multiplies primes of neighbour ranks to refine atom invariants: a prime-product molecular graph code used for canonical ordering, not related to partitioning

candidates.title: Atomic ring invariant and Modified CANON extended connectivity algorithm for symmetry perception in molecular graphs and rigorous canonicalization of SMILES (Krotko 2020)
candidates.basis: prime products for neighbour ranks and ring sizes in canonicalization; paper relates the encoding to no physicochemical property (checked on PMC7439248)

candidates.title: QSPR Modeling of Lipid-Water Partition Coefficient by Optimization of Correlation Weights of Local Graph Invariants (Toropov, Roy 2003)
candidates.basis: nearest mathematical form: atom-additive descriptor built from element-type and vertex-degree weights correlated with log P, but the weights are fitted to the property, not fixed prime logarithms

candidates.title: Evaluation of Molecular Connectivity Indices as a Predictive Method of log Kow for Different Classes of Chemicals (Finizio, Sicbaldi, Vighi 1995)
candidates.basis: degree-based indices with element-specific valence deltas regressed on measured log Kow across chemical classes; different functional form, no prime code

candidates.title: On quantitative structure-property relationship (QSPR) analysis of physicochemical properties and anti-hepatitis prescription drugs using a linear regression model (Mahboob et al. 2024)
candidates.basis: 14 element-blind degree-based indices vs LogP for 16 drugs (r 0.68-0.91); no element weighting, no prime code

candidates.title: Structural Relationship Study of Octanol-Water Partitioning Coefficients and Total Biodegradation of Barbiturate Medicines by Randic Descriptor (Taherpour et al. 2012)
candidates.basis: single degree-based index (Randic) related to log Kow within one drug class; not a prime or element-weighted code

candidates.title: Estimating the Octanol/Water Partition Coefficient for Aliphatic Organic Compounds Using Semi-Empirical Electrotopological Index (Souza et al. 2011)
candidates.basis: one graph-derived index regressed on log P of 131 aliphatics; index built from semi-empirical atomic charges, not a prime-power code

candidates.title: Evaluation of the Usefulness of Topological Indices for Predicting Selected Physicochemical Properties of Bioactive Substances with Anti-Androgenic and Hypouricemic Activity (Wardecki et al. 2023)
candidates.basis: Gutman M/Mv, Randic and Wiener indices vs lipophilicity of a small drug set; additive degree indices, no prime code

candidates.title: Use of TLC and Computational Methods to Determine Lipophilicity Parameters of Selected Neuroleptics (Klimoszek et al. 2025)
candidates.basis: Gutman M and connectivity indices correlated with calculated logP of five neuroleptics; additive degree indices, no prime code

candidates.title: Vertex-Edge-Weighted Molecular Graphs: A Study on Topological Indices and Their Relevance to Physicochemical Properties of Drugs Used in Cancer Treatment (Sorgun, Birgin 2025)
candidates.basis: degree-based indices with vertex/edge weights from atomic properties (closest element-weighted degree form); log P not among the properties named in the abstract or search excerpts

candidates.title: Leveraging topological indices and machine learning for advanced prediction of antidepressant drug properties (Zhang et al. 2026)
candidates.basis: eight multiplicative degree indices, but properties modelled are BP, MP, Tc, Vc and MR; log P not modelled (checked on PMC12848129)

candidates.title: Sharp Bounds on the Generalized Multiplicative First Zagreb Index of Graphs with Application to QSPR Modeling (Hayat, Asmat 2023)
candidates.basis: multiplicative index applied only to pi-electron energy of benzenoid hydrocarbons (Crossref abstract)

candidates.title: Molecular Hashkeys: A Novel Method for Molecular Characterization and Its Application for Predicting Important Pharmaceutical Properties of Molecules (Ghuloum, Sage, Jain 1999)
candidates.basis: predicts log P from a 3D surface-similarity vector called a hashkey; not an integer code of the molecular graph

candidates.title: Atom/Fragment Contribution Method for Estimating Octanol-Water Partition Coefficients (Meylan, Howard 1995)
candidates.basis: atom-additive like the code's logarithm, but constants are fitted fragment values; no fixed graph code

candidates.title: On molecular identification numbers (Randic 1984)
candidates.basis: path-weighted numeric graph identifiers for discrimination; not prime-based, no partitioning

candidates.title: Molecular ID numbers: by design (Randic 1986)
candidates.basis: numeric graph identifiers; not prime-based, no partitioning

candidates.title: On Unique Numbering of Atoms and Unique Codes for Molecular Graphs (Randic 1975)
candidates.basis: adjacency-matrix code for canonical numbering; not prime-based, no property

candidates.title: Unique gating strategy identifier based on the Prime Population System and Godel Numbers (2025)
